source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for PR #251 (branch fix/177-interrupt-wakes-atomic-wait at commit 871ecfabacc14d43045d295960fbd062c24f53b8, the merge of the PR head 848e64b853e66e1cf769c2321ef17adbfe4b2e29 with main e46cd8d66dfcf415f5a0a9521a52e70f5a9cf376; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45051812925 and 45051827578 against the branch and pull-request run 45051722003, which built the same merge tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #251 (#177, interrupt() does not wake a guest parked in an indefinite memory.atomic.wait). The PR adds the interrupt wake path to the telomere library: a fourth waiter state (INTERRUPTED) with a CAS claim and wait_result_interruptible racing notify / timeout / interrupt in crates/telomere/src/common/memory.rs, the Interrupted completion plumbing in runtime/memory_effect.rs and runtime/scheduler.rs, and - compiled only under the threads feature - the broadcast Notify in common/metering.rs (MeteringState gains interrupt_notify, MeteringHandle::interrupt() broadcasts after the flag store, and wait_for_interrupt registers interest and re-checks the flag so no wakeup is lost). The library is linked into every embedder configuration except baseline, so the gated growth is nearly uniform (release stripped .text +608 B in core, component, wasi, core-nosimd and core-jit, stripped file +1,016 B with component +1,000 B; release-size stripped .text +272 B with core-jit +256 B, stripped file +392..+424 B), the baseline configuration is unchanged, and wasi-threads grows most because the threads-only metering broadcast path lands there (release +3,520 B stripped file / +2,384 B stripped .text; release-size +1,760 B / +992 B). 24 of 28 gated series changed; the 4 unchanged series are the baseline configuration's. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, 'Size regression gate (#164)'.
